title: Je le vois
en: Object pronouns: le, la, les, me, te…
intro: To avoid repeating a noun, French replaces it with a small word that goes **before the verb**: *Tu vois Léa ? — Oui, je **la** vois.* These are the **direct object pronouns**: **me, te, le, la, nous, vous, les**.

cases.label: the direct object
cases.rule: The **direct object** comes right after the verb, with **no preposition**. It answers *what?* or *who?*: *Je prends **le bus**. J'aime **Léa**.* That's what a pronoun can replace.

cases.label: le, la, les
cases.rule: **le** replaces a masculine noun, **la** a feminine noun, **les** a plural noun, for things or people: *Je prends le bus → je **le** prends. Je vois Léa → je **la** vois. Je cherche mes clés → je **les** cherche.*

cases.label: l' before a vowel
cases.rule: **le** and **la** become **l'** before a vowel or a silent h: *J'aime la musique → je **l'**aime. J'attends Hugo → je **l'**attends.* **les** never changes: *je **les** aime* (with a /z/ sound).

cases.label: me, te, nous, vous
cases.rule: For people: **me** (me), **te** (you), **nous** (us), **vous** (you): *Tu **m'**aimes ? Je **t'**appelle ce soir. Il **nous** invite.* **me** and **te** become **m'** and **t'** before a vowel.

cases.label: before the verb
cases.rule: The pronoun goes **before the conjugated verb**: *je **le** vois, tu **la** connais ?* In the negative, **ne** comes first: *je **ne le** vois **pas***.

cases.label: with an infinitive
cases.rule: With two verbs, the pronoun goes **before the infinitive**: *je vais **la** voir, tu peux **les** prendre, je veux **le** faire*.

cases.label: in commands
cases.rule: In a positive command, the pronoun comes **after** the verb, with a hyphen: *Regarde-**le** ! Prends-**les** !* **me** and **te** become **moi** and **toi**: *Aide-**moi** !* In a negative command, it goes back before the verb: *Ne **le** regarde pas !*

cases.label: regarder, écouter, attendre, chercher
cases.rule: These verbs take a direct object in French, but a preposition in English: **regarder** (look at), **écouter** (listen to), **attendre** (wait for), **chercher** (look for), **payer** (pay for): *J'attends le bus → je **l'**attends.*

sections.title: 1. What is a direct object?
text: The direct object is the thing or person **right after the verb**, with no **à** or **de** in between. Find it, and you can replace it with a pronoun.

examples.en: Hugo is looking for his keys.

sections.title: 2. le, la, les

examples.fr: Ta robe ? {Je la trouve|cod-le-la-les} très jolie.
examples.en: Your dress? I think it's very pretty.

examples.fr: Les enfants ? {Je les vois|cod-le-la-les} dans le jardin.
examples.en: The children? I can see them in the garden.

sections.tip: The pronoun has the same gender and number as the noun it replaces: **le** bus → **le**, **la** télé → **la**, **les** clés → **les**.

sections.title: 3. l' before a vowel
sections.tip: **les** before a vowel keeps its **s** and links with a /z/: *je les‿aime* /ʒə le.zɛm/.

examples.en: Can you hear me? Yes, I can hear you!
Léa is waiting for us outside the cinema.

sections.title: 5. Before the verb
text: The pronoun sits **just before the conjugated verb**, in statements, questions and negatives.

examples.fr: Ce film ? {Je ne le connais pas|cod-place}.
examples.en: This film? I don't know it.
Your jacket? Are you taking it?

sections.title: 6. With an infinitive
text: When there are two verbs (**aller, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir** + infinitive), the pronoun goes before the **infinitive**, the verb it belongs to.

head: French
English
rows: I'm going to see her tomorrow.
I'm not going to buy it.

examples.en: This cake? I'm going to eat it!
Your glasses? You need to look for them!

sections.title: 7. In commands

examples.en: Your jacket? Take it, it's raining!

examples.fr: {Ne le mange pas|cod-imperative}, c'est pour Lou !
examples.en: Don't eat it, it's for Lou!

sections.tip: After the verb: **moi, toi** (not *me, te*): *Écoute-**moi** ! Lève-**toi** !*

sections.title: 8. regarder, écouter, attendre, chercher
text: In English you *look **at***, *listen **to***, *wait **for*** and *look **for***. In French, no preposition: the person or thing is a direct object.

head: English
French
rows: Je regarde la télé. Je la regarde.
listen to the radio → listen to it
wait for the bus → wait for it
look for my keys → look for them
Je cherche mes clés. Je les cherche.

examples.fr: Le bus ? {Je l'attends|cod-verbs} depuis vingt minutes !
examples.en: The bus? I've been waiting for it for twenty minutes!

examples.fr: Cette chanson ? {Je l'écoute|cod-verbs} tous les jours.
examples.en: This song? I listen to it every day.

mistakes.why: With an infinitive, the pronoun goes before the infinitive.

story.title: Où sont mes clés ?
story.en: Monday morning at Hugo's: he can't find anything. Luckily, his sister is there.

lines.fr: Lundi matin, chez Hugo. Léa a dormi chez son frère, sur le canapé.
lines.en: Monday morning, at Hugo's. Léa slept at her brother's, on the sofa.

lines.fr: Il est huit heures. Hugo cherche {ses affaires|cod-what} partout… comme toujours.
lines.en: It's eight o'clock. Hugo is looking everywhere for his things… as always.
Léa! My keys! Can you see them?

lines.fr: Oui, {je les vois|cod-place} : elles sont sur la table. {Prends-les|cod-imperative} !
lines.en: Yes, I can see them: they're on the table. Take them!

lines.fr: Et mon téléphone ? {Je ne le trouve pas|cod-place} !
lines.en: And my phone? I can't find it!

lines.fr: {Je l'appelle|cod-elision}… {Écoute-le|cod-verbs} : il sonne dans la cuisine !
lines.en: I'll call it… Listen to it: it's ringing in the kitchen!

lines.fr: Merci ! Et mes lunettes ? {Je les cherche|cod-verbs} depuis dix minutes !
lines.en: Thanks! And my glasses? I've been looking for them for ten minutes!

lines.fr: Tes lunettes ? Hugo… {tu les portes|cod-le-la-les} sur ta tête !
lines.en: Your glasses? Hugo… you're wearing them on your head!

lines.fr: Ah oui ! Bon, je pars. {Tu m'attends|cod-me-te} ce soir ? On mange ensemble ?
lines.en: Oh yes! Right, I'm off. Will you wait for me tonight? Shall we eat together?

lines.fr: D'accord, {je t'attends|cod-me-te}. Et ta veste ? {Tu ne la prends pas|cod-place} ? Il pleut !
lines.en: OK, I'll wait for you. And your jacket? Aren't you taking it? It's raining!

lines.fr: Ma veste ? {Je vais la chercher|cod-inf}… Ah, [la|la-pron] voilà, sur la chaise !
lines.en: My jacket? I'll go and look for it… Ah, there it is, on the chair!

lines.fr: Hugo part. Deux minutes plus tard, il revient.
lines.en: Hugo leaves. Two minutes later, he comes back.

lines.fr: Léa ! Mon sac ! {Tu peux le prendre|cod-inf} ? Il est à côté de la porte !
lines.en: Léa! My bag! Can you grab it? It's next to the door!

lines.fr: Tiens ! Et {ne m'appelle pas|cod-imperative} à midi : je dors !
lines.en: Here you go! And don't call me at noon: I'll be asleep!

lines.fr: {Je t'aime|cod-me-te}, petite sœur ! Tu me sauves la vie !
lines.en: I love you, little sister! You're a lifesaver!

lines.fr: La porte se ferme. Léa sourit… puis elle voit le portefeuille de Hugo sur la table.
lines.en: The door closes. Léa smiles… then she sees Hugo's wallet on the table.

lines.fr: Oh non ! {Il l'oublie|cod-elision} tous les jours ! Bon… {je vais l'appeler|cod-inf}.
lines.en: Oh no! He forgets it every day! Right… I'll call him.

lines.fr: Dans le bus, Hugo cherche son portefeuille… et {ne le trouve pas|cod-place}.
lines.en: On the bus, Hugo looks for his wallet… and can't find it.

quiz.q: In « Je regarde le film », the direct object is…
Which sentence has a direct object?
Tu prends le bus ? — Oui, je ___ prends.
quiz.en: Are you taking the bus? — Yes, I'm taking it.

quiz.q: Tu vois Léa ? — Oui, je ___ vois.
quiz.en: Can you see Léa? — Yes, I can see her.

quiz.q: Tu connais Paul et Anne ? — Oui, je ___ connais.
quiz.en: Do you know Paul and Anne? — Yes, I know them.

quiz.q: Tu aimes la musique ? — Oui, je ___aime.
quiz.en: Do you like music? — Yes, I love it.
Are you waiting for Hugo? — Yes, I'm waiting for him.
Can you hear me? — Yes, I can hear you fine.
This film? I don't know it.

quiz.en: Your keys? You need to look for them!
Your jacket? Take it, it's raining!

quiz.en: This film is rubbish. Don't watch it!
